ErrorCode.description:
Error code. Every failed response sets `error.code` to one of these stable strings; branch on it rather than on the HTTP status.

| `OK` | 200 | Reserved; never returned on a failed request. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A parameter is missing, has the wrong type, or failed validation; `message` usually names the field. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | The request breaks a business rule or conflicts with the current state of an object; `message` says which. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The body is not sent as `application/json`. |
| `ResourceNotFound` | 400 | The referenced object does not exist in this account or was deleted. Returned as HTTP 400, not 404. |
| `NoLicense` | 400 | The account's plan does not include the feature, a plan quota is used up, the plan has expired, or credits are insufficient. |
| `ReferenceExist` | 400 | The object is still referenced by other objects, so it cannot be deleted. |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 | The APP Key is missing, invalid, or deleted. |
| `BalanceNotEnough` | 402 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `AccessDenied` | 403 | The APP Key's permission scope or the creator's role does not allow this operation or object. |
| `RouteNotFound` | 404 | No operation matches the HTTP method and path. |
| `MethodNotAllowed` | 405 | The path exists but not for this HTTP method. |
| `UndonedOrderExist` | 409 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `EntityTooLarge` | 413 | The request body exceeds the size limit. |
| `RequestLocked` | 423 | Console-only (sign-in protection); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestVerifyRequired` | 428 | Console-only (verification code); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `DangerousOperation` | 428 | Console-only (MFA for high-risk actions); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestTooFrequently` | 429 | A rate limit was hit; wait for the `Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay` response header (seconds) before retrying. |
| `InternalError` | 500 | Unexpected server error; retry with backoff and include `request_id` when reporting. |
| `ServiceUnavailable` | 503 | A backend dependency is overloaded or unavailable; retry with backoff. |

ListRemoteConfigHistoryRequest.description: Remote configuration history request. Newest first by default.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

limit.description: Page size. `0` or a negative value means 20; values above 100 are treated as 100.

orderby.description:
Sort field:

- `updated_at`: publish time (default).
- `version`: version number.

Any other value falls back to `updated_at`.

p.description: Zero-based page index; offset is p multiplied by limit.

has_next_page.description: `true` when more versions remain after this page.

items.description: Versions on this page, newest first by default. Empty array when the application has never been configured.

PreviewRemoteConfigRequest.description: Preview request. Omit `config` to preview the currently live configuration.

app_version.description: App version the simulated client reports, compared exactly with rules' `match.app_version` (no range or prefix matching). Omitted = not reported.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

config.description: Draft configuration to evaluate, validated like `POST /rum/application/remote-config/update`. Omit to evaluate the live configuration.

env.description: Environment the simulated client reports, compared exactly with rules' `match.env`. Omitted = not reported, so rules that test `env` cannot match.

sdk.description: SDK identifier the simulated client reports, e.g. `web@2.4.1`, compared exactly with rules' `match.sdk`. Omitted = not reported.

PreviewRemoteConfigResponse.description: Values the simulated client would receive.

hit_rule_index.description: 0-based index into `config.rules` of the first rule that matched, or `-1` when no rule matched (only `default` applied) or the configuration is disabled or absent.

values.description: `default` merged with the matching rule's `set`. Fields set by neither are omitted; an empty object means the client keeps all its init values.

RemoteConfig.description: The whole per-application remote configuration. A change reaches an SDK asynchronously and is applied when that SDK creates its next session, so a running session never flips a decision mid-flight.

activation.description: How a change lands on a client that is already running: `next_session` (the default, and what an empty value means) leaves running sessions untouched and applies the change to new sessions; `immediate` ends the running session as soon as the change arrives so a new session starts under the new configuration.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value: string, number, boolean, array or object.

custom.description: Free-form key/value map that SDKs hand to the host app verbatim; the platform does not interpret it. At most 5 keys, each key 1–64 bytes, each value valid JSON of at most 4 KB nested at most 3 levels, 16 KB in total. Anyone holding the public client token can read it. Omitted from responses when empty.

default.description: Values every client receives unless a matching rule overrides them.

enabled.description: Kill switch. When `false` the SDK config endpoint returns no values and SDKs fall back to their init values; `default` and `rules` are kept. Treated as `false` when omitted.

refresh_on_foreground.description: If `true`, clients re-check the configuration when they return to the foreground instead of waiting for the next poll. Default `false`; omitted from responses when `false`.

rules.description: Targeting rules, evaluated in order; the first match wins. At most 20. Can be `null` when the configuration was saved without rules.

config.description: The configuration content that went live under this version.

content_hash.description: Fingerprint of the stored configuration: the first 16 hex characters of its SHA-256. Versions with equal hashes have identical content. Can be empty for older versions.

equivalent_to.description: Earliest retained version with the same `content_hash`, e.g. the version a revert restored. Omitted when this version is itself the earliest.

reason.description: Free-text note (not an enum) sent as `reason` when the version was published or reverted; `""` when none was given.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the version was published.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who published the version.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the member who published the version at publish time, truncated to 128 characters.

version.description: Version number, unique within the application.

RemoteConfigRule.description: One targeting rule: when every `match` condition holds, `set` overrides `default`. The first matching rule wins and evaluation stops there; rule order is the priority. `set` must set at least one value.

match.description: Conditions on what the SDK reports in its config request, combined with AND and compared as exact strings. Keys are limited to `env`, `app_version` and `sdk`; values are 1–256 bytes. A key the SDK does not report never matches.

RemoteConfigValues.description: The SDK knobs a configuration can set. Every field is optional: a value absent from both rule and default is omitted from the SDK response, which tells the SDK to keep its init value.

defaultPrivacyLevel.description:
How Session Replay masks a page by default:

- `mask`: replaces text and hides input values.
- `mask-user-input`: keeps page text but hides what users type.
- `allow`: records the page as it is; content already uploaded cannot be masked later.

sessionOnError.description: Keep sessions the session sample rate did not draw when they report an error; applies only to sessions that rate missed, so it does nothing alongside a rate of 100.

sessionReplayOnError.description: The same switch for Session Replay: un-sampled sessions still record and upload their recording only when the session errors.

sessionReplaySampleRate.description: Percentage of sessions that record Session Replay (0–100).

traceSampleRate.description: Percentage of sessions that inject trace headers into their requests (0–100). Decided per session: a session traces all of its requests or none.

RevertRemoteConfigRequest.description: Republish an earlier version's content under a new version number.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

reason.description: Optional free-text note (not an enum), at most 255 characters, stored verbatim and returned as `reason` by `POST /rum/application/remote-config/history/list`. The server does not fill it in when omitted.

version.description: Version to restore. Must be one of the retained versions listed by `POST /rum/application/remote-config/history/list`.
New version number created by the revert (previous highest version + 1).

channel_ids.description: On-call channel IDs that receive the alerts; used only when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`. Kept as a draft in `webhook` mode. Can be `null` when never set.

delivery_mode.description: Alert delivery channel: `oncall` routes alert events through Flashduty On-call, `webhook` POSTs them directly to `webhook_url`. An empty value is treated as `oncall`, and on create/update it is persisted as the deployment default (`webhook` on RUM-only on-premises deployments, `oncall` otherwise). Omitted when empty (legacy rows).

enabled.description: Whether alerting is on. `false` turns alerting off; with `false`, `webhook_url` is not checked.

integration_id.description: Associated on-call integration ID (read-only, auto-assigned on save when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`).

webhook_url.description: URL that receives alert events when `delivery_mode` is `webhook`. Required in that mode while `enabled` is `true`; must use `http` or `https`, and on Flashduty cloud must not resolve to a private, loopback, link-local or reserved address. Ignored in `oncall` mode. Omitted from responses when empty.

name.description: Column name or alias as written in `sql`; `ts` for the bucket column of `time_series` queries.

nullable.description: Whether values in this column may be `null`. `true` when the driver cannot tell.

type.description: Column type name as reported by the database driver, such as `VARCHAR`, `BIGINT`, `DOUBLE` or `DATETIME`. It depends on the selected column or expression, so the set is open; use it as a hint for parsing `values`.

disable_sampling.description: When `true`, the query always runs on the full data and the response never carries `sampling`. When `false` (default), the server may sample aggregate queries over large time windows.

dql.description: Optional RUM DQL filter. It is translated and `AND`-ed into the `WHERE` clause of `sql`. A DQL parse error is reported in this query's `error` entry.

format.description: Output format. `table` returns rows; `time_series` returns bucketed time-series rows.

id.description: Client-supplied query ID. The same value is used as the key in the response object.

interval.description: Minimum time-bucket width in **milliseconds** for `time_series` queries. Default 3600 (3.6 seconds). The effective width is the smallest step of a fixed ladder that is at least this value and at least the window length divided by `max_points`; it is returned as `interval`. Ignored for `table` queries.

max_points.description: Upper bound on the number of buckets for `time_series` queries. Default 1226. The bucket width grows so that the window holds at most this many buckets. Ignored for `table` queries.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor from a previous response's `search_after_ctx`, to fetch the next page of the same `table` query. Only used by non-aggregate queries with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET`. An invalid value makes this query fail.

sql.description: RUM SQL `SELECT` statement. `FROM` names a scope table (`sessions`, `views`, `actions`, `errors`, `resources`, `long_tasks`, `vitals`, `issues`, `sourcemaps`); columns are `field_key` values from `POST /rum/field/list`. The server adds the account and time-range filters.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone name, such as `Asia/Shanghai`, used to align `time_series` bucket boundaries to local time. Defaults to UTC alignment. Ignored for `table` queries; an unknown name fails the request with `InvalidParameter`.

RumDataQueryOutput.description: Result for one query. Failed subqueries populate `error`; successful ones populate `data`.

data.description: Query result. Omitted when the query failed.

error.description: Set when this query failed after request validation (unknown table or column, invalid `dql` or `search_after_ctx`, database error). The code is always `InternalError`. Omitted when the query succeeded.

RumDataQueryRequest.description: Batch of RUM data queries over a bounded time range.

end_time.description: End of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum 31-day span.

queries.description: Queries to execute concurrently. 1 to 10 queries are allowed.

start_time.description: Start of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds.

RumDataQueryResponse.description: Map from request query ID to that query's result or error.

RumDataQueryResult.description: Rows and metadata returned by one RUM data query.

fields.description: Column metadata, one entry per returned column, in the same order as `values`. For `time_series` queries the first column is `ts`.

interval.description: Effective time-bucket width in **milliseconds** used by a `time_series` query. Omitted for `table` queries.

sampling.description: Sampling metadata. Omitted when the query did not use sampling.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page of a non-aggregate `table` query with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET`. Present only when this page returned as many rows as the `LIMIT`; omitted otherwise.

values.description: Result values in column-major order: `values[i]` is the list of every row's value for column `fields[i]`. A column is `null` when the query returned no rows. Datetime values are returned as RFC 3339 strings.

RumDataSamplingDecision.description: Sampling metadata returned when the query engine used sampled data.

enabled.description: Whether sampling was applied. Always `true` here — the `sampling` object is omitted entirely when sampling was not used.

scale_factor.description: Multiplier applied to scale sampled results back to estimated full values. `COUNT`, `SUM` and `COUNT(DISTINCT)` columns in `values` are already multiplied by it; other aggregates are returned as computed on the sample.

RumErrorIngestionCreateRequest.description: Fields for creating a new error ingestion rule.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

description.description: Rule description, up to 512 characters. Defaults to an empty string.

filters.description: Conditions (OR-of-ANDs) that select errors. A matched error is still stored but is not grouped into any issue.

rule_id.description: ID assigned to the new rule.

rule_name.description: Echo of the created rule's name.

RumErrorIngestionFilterCondition.description: A single filter condition matched against one error field.

key.description: Field to match. One of `error.usr_id`, `error.usr_email`, `error.error_type`, `error.error_message`, `error.error_stack`, `error.view_url`, `error.env`, `error.version`, `error.service`, `error.browser_name`, `error.browser_version`, `error.fingerprint`, `error.is_crash` (value `true` or `false`), or a `context.`-prefixed path into the error's custom context. Context objects are flattened with dots up to 3 levels (`context.a.b.c`); a deeper object is compared as its JSON text, and array values can't be matched.

oper.description:
Match mode:
- `IN`: matches when the field value matches any entry in `vals`. A context field the error doesn't carry never matches.
- `NOTIN`: matches when the field value matches none of `vals`. A context field the error doesn't carry always matches.

vals.description: Values to match against, at least 1 entry. Each entry is one of: an exact, case-sensitive string; a wildcard pattern using `*`/`?` that must match the whole value; a regexp wrapped in `/` (matches anywhere in the value unless anchored); `cidr:<range>` (the value is parsed as an IP); or `num:lt|le|gt|ge:<number>` (the value is parsed as a number, non-numeric values don't match).

RumErrorIngestionHistoryItem.description: A snapshot of every rule for the application at one history version.

rules.description: The application's complete non-deleted rule list as it was just before the change that created this version. Empty for the version created by the application's first rule.

updated_at.description: Time of the change that created this version, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_by.description: Member ID of the person who made the change that created this version.

updated_by_name.description: Display name of that member at the time of the change.

version.description: History version number, starting at 1 and incremented by every write. Pass it to `POST /rum/error-ingestion/rules/history/revert`.

RumErrorIngestionHistoryListRequest.description: Query parameters for paginating an application's rule history.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

asc.description: `true` sorts ascending; `false` (default) sorts descending, newest first.

limit.description: Page size. Default 20; values above 100 are clamped to 100, and values of 0 or below fall back to 20.

orderby.description:
Sort column:
- `updated_at`: time of the change that created the version (default).
- `version`: version number.
Any other value falls back to `updated_at`.

has_next_page.description: `true` when more versions exist after this page.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

filters.description: OR-of-ANDs filter structure: the outer array is OR'd, each inner array is AND'd. A rule matches an error when at least one inner AND-group fully matches. An empty outer array never matches; an empty inner group matches every error.

severity.description: Severity to assign to errors matching this rule.

priority.description: Evaluation order assigned to the new rule (always the current lowest precedence, i.e. current max + 1).

rule_id.description: ID of the newly created rule.

rule_name.description: Echo of the rule's display name.

RumPresetSeverityRuleFilterCondition.description: One filter condition within an AND group.

key.description:
Filter attribute key. Only these Error-level attributes are supported for preset severity rules.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `error.usr_id` | User ID |
| `error.usr_email` | User email |
| `error.view_url` | Full URL of the page where the error occurred |
| `error.view_url_path` | URL path of the page where the error occurred |
| `error.error_type` | Error type |
| `error.error_message` | Error message |
| `error.env` | Environment (e.g. production/staging) |
| `error.service` | Service name |
| `error.device_type` | Device type |
| `error.os_name` | Operating system name |
| `error.browser_name` | Browser name |
| `error.is_crash` | Whether the error is a crash, compared as the string `true` or `false` |

oper.description: Match semantics: `IN` matches when the attribute value matches any of `vals`; `NOTIN` matches when it matches none of them. An attribute the error does not carry is compared as an empty string.

vals.description: Values to match against; at least one, none empty. Each entry is one of: an exact, case-sensitive whole-value match; a wildcard pattern with `*`/`?` (whole value); a regular expression wrapped in `/.../` (matches anywhere in the value unless anchored with `^`/`$`); `cidr:<network>` for IP-shaped values, e.g. `cidr:10.0.0.0/8`; or a numeric comparison `num:<op>:<number>` with `op` one of `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`, e.g. `num:gt:100`. For `error.is_crash`, use `true` or `false`.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Send 1 to 10 queries in one request; each query `id` becomes a key in the response object.
- `start_time` and `end_time` are Unix epoch milliseconds, at most 31 days apart. The server adds the time-range and account filters itself; you do not need them in `sql`.
- `FROM` names a RUM scope table: `sessions`, `views`, `actions`, `errors`, `resources`, `long_tasks`, `vitals`, `issues` or `sourcemaps` (the singular form is also accepted). Column names are the `field_key` values returned by `POST /rum/field/list`.
- A query whose top-level `AND` conditions pin `application_id` (`=` or `IN`) must name applications the caller can read: a private application the caller's team does not own fails the whole request with `AccessDenied`, an unknown one with `ResourceNotFound`, and one request may name at most 50 distinct applications. A query that names no application silently skips the private applications the caller cannot read.
- Malformed SQL, an invalid `time_zone` or an out-of-range time window fails the whole request with `InvalidParameter`. A query that fails later (unknown table or column, invalid `dql`, invalid `search_after_ctx`, database error) only sets `error` on its own entry, with code `InternalError`; the other queries still return `data`.
- `values` is column-major: `values[i]` holds every row's value of column `fields[i]`.
- `table` queries return at most 1,000 rows; a missing `LIMIT` or one above 1,000 is replaced with 1,000. A non-aggregate query with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET` returns `search_after_ctx` when the page is full — send it back with the same `sql` to get the next page.
- `time_series` queries get a `ts` column prepended (bucket start, Unix milliseconds), grouped and ordered by it. The bucket width, returned as `interval` in milliseconds, is the smallest step from a fixed ladder (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 ms; 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 s; 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min; 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 h; 1, 2, 3, 7 d; 30, 60, 90, 180 d) that is at least both `interval` and the window length divided by `max_points`.
- On large time windows an aggregate query may run on sampled data; the response then carries `sampling`, and `COUNT`, `SUM` and `COUNT(DISTINCT)` columns are already multiplied by `scale_factor`. Set `disable_sampling: true` to always query the full data.

- A cursor is returned whenever a page is full (`limit` segments), so the last page can be empty.
- `limit` accepts 1-99; values of 100 or more are rejected.
- If the session belongs to a private application the caller cannot access, the call returns `AccessDenied` ("You do not have permission to access this application").
- A page with no segments returns an empty result. Segments uploaded moments ago may not be indexed yet; the call then returns `ResourceNotFound` ("Replay segments are not available yet. Please retry shortly"), so retry after a short wait.
